home.title: Mic & Webcam Test: Free Online Microphone and Camera Check
home.description: Mic test and webcam test in one click. Live mic level meter, recording and playback, camera resolution and FPS check. Free, private, nothing is uploaded.
home.lead: Test your microphone, webcam and speakers in seconds. No sign‑up, no downloads, nothing leaves your device.

article.h: How to test your microphone and webcam online
p: MicTest+ checks your microphone, webcam and speakers right in your browser. Press the button under the headline and allow access when your browser asks. No app to install, no account to create.
ol: Click "Test everything" (or start the mic or camera test on its own).
When the browser asks for permission, choose "Allow".
Speak normally. The level meter and waveform should move with your voice.
Look at the camera preview. Check the image, resolution and frame rate.
Play the left/right tones to confirm your speakers or headphones work.

article.h: What the results mean
p: The microphone meter shows the loudness of your input in decibels (dB) relative to the maximum the device can capture. Silence usually sits below −60 dB, normal speech at arm's length lands between −35 and −15 dB, and anything that touches 0 dB will clip and sound distorted.

For the camera, the resolution (for example 1280 × 720 or 1920 × 1080) tells you how much detail you get. The frame rate (FPS) tells you how smooth the motion is. 30 FPS is standard for video calls. Many webcams drop to 15 FPS in dim light, so add light if your FPS is low.

article.h: Test before Zoom, Teams, Google Meet or Discord
p: A quick check before an important meeting, interview, online class or stream saves you from the classic "can you hear me?" moment. Choose the same microphone and camera here that you plan to use in Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Skype, Discord or OBS. If they work on MicTest+, they work in the browser, so any remaining problem is in that app's own audio or video settings.

article.h: Microphone or camera not working? Quick fixes
ul: Allow access: click the lock or camera icon next to the address bar and set Camera and Microphone to "Allow", then reload.
Close other apps: Zoom, Teams, OBS or another browser tab can lock the camera so nothing else can use it.
Pick the right device: use the drop-down to switch between built-in, USB and Bluetooth devices.
Check system privacy settings: on Windows open Settings → Privacy & security → Camera / Microphone; on macOS open System Settings → Privacy & Security.
Look for hardware switches: many laptops have a camera shutter or a mute key, and headsets often have an inline mute switch.
Update drivers or restart: a reboot clears most "device not found" errors.

article.h: Is it private?
p: Yes. Everything runs locally using standard browser technology (WebRTC getUserMedia and the Web Audio API). Your voice and video are never sent to a server, never stored and never seen by anyone. Recordings and snapshots exist only in your browser until you close the tab or choose to download them.

faq.q: Is this mic and webcam test free?
faq.a: Yes, it is completely free with no sign‑up, no limits and nothing to install.

faq.q: Is my audio or video recorded or uploaded?
faq.a: No. Everything happens inside your browser. Nothing is uploaded or stored on any server.

faq.q: My browser didn't ask for permission. What do I do?
faq.a: Click the camera or lock icon in the address bar, set Camera and Microphone to "Allow", and reload the page. On iPhone go to Settings → Safari → Camera / Microphone and choose "Ask" or "Allow".

faq.q: Why does my camera show a black screen?
faq.a: Another app may be using the camera, a privacy shutter may be closed, or the selected resolution isn't supported. Close other apps, open the shutter, try another resolution, or pick another camera from the list.

faq.q: Does it work on iPhone and Android?
faq.a: Yes. It works in Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Samsung Internet on iOS and Android. Use "Switch camera" to test both the front and back cameras.

faq.q: Which browsers are supported?
faq.a: Any modern browser: Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, Opera, Brave and Samsung Internet. The page has to be opened over HTTPS for camera and mic access.

mic.title: Mic Test: Free Online Microphone Test (Instant & Private)
mic.description: Free online mic test and mic check. See a live level meter in dB, waveform and spectrum, then record and play back your voice. Works with any mic or headset.
mic.lead: Check if your microphone works in seconds. Speak and watch the level meter, then record and listen back to how you sound.

article.h: How to test your microphone
ol: Click "Start mic test" and allow microphone access.
Pick your microphone from the drop-down if you have more than one.
Talk at your normal volume and watch the meter and waveform.
Press "Record 5s", then play the clip back to hear exactly what others hear.

article.h: What is a good microphone level?
p: Aim for peaks between −20 dB and −10 dB while speaking normally. Below −45 dB the other side will struggle to hear you: move closer or raise the input gain. If the meter keeps hitting the red zone near 0 dB, your voice will clip and sound harsh, so lower the gain or move the mic back a little.

The "Dominant frequency" value shows the strongest pitch the mic picks up. Most voices sit between 85 Hz and 255 Hz. A constant reading at 50 Hz or 60 Hz with no one speaking usually points to electrical hum from a cable or power supply.

article.h: Microphone not working? Try this
ul: Browser permission: click the lock icon in the address bar → Microphone → Allow, then reload.

Windows 10/11: Settings → System → Sound → Input. Select your mic and check the "Input volume". Also open Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone and turn on access for desktop apps and your browser.
macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone → enable your browser. Then System Settings → Sound → Input to choose the device and input level.
iPhone / iPad: Settings → Safari (or Chrome) → Microphone → Allow.
Android: long-press the browser icon → App info → Permissions → Microphone → Allow.
Headsets: check the inline mute switch, and make sure the plug is in the mic (pink) jack or that you're using a 4-pole TRRS connector.
Bluetooth headsets: some switch to a low-quality "hands-free" mode when the mic is active. That is normal behavior, not a fault.

article.h: Tips for clearer sound on calls
ul: Keep the mic 10–20 cm (4–8 in) from your mouth and slightly off-axis to avoid pops.
Use "Hear myself" with headphones to monitor background noise in real time.
Soft furnishings such as curtains, rugs and a sofa reduce echo far more than any software filter.
Leave echo cancellation and noise suppression on for calls; turn them off only for music recording.

faq.q: How do I know if my microphone is working?
faq.a: Start the test and speak. If the level meter and waveform move with your voice and the status turns green, your mic works. Record a 5-second clip and play it back to confirm the quality.

faq.q: Can I use this as a quick mic check before a call?
faq.a: Yes. Open the page, press Start and say a few words. If the meter moves and the status turns green, your mic check is done. It takes about five seconds.

faq.q: Why is my mic so quiet?
faq.a: The input gain is probably low. Raise the input volume in your operating system's sound settings, move closer to the mic, and check that you selected the right device in the drop-down.

faq.q: Why does my microphone pick up an echo?
faq.a: Usually your speakers are feeding back into the mic. Use headphones, lower the speaker volume, and keep echo cancellation enabled in your calling app.

faq.q: Can I test a USB or Bluetooth microphone?
faq.a: Yes. Connect it, press Refresh in the device list if needed, and choose it from the microphone drop-down.

faq.q: Can I download my test recording?
faq.a: Yes. After recording, press Download to save the clip. It is created in your browser and never uploaded.

webcam.title: Webcam Test: Check Your Camera Online (Resolution & FPS)
webcam.description: Free online webcam test and cam test. See your live camera, real resolution, FPS, aspect ratio and brightness. Take snapshots and record clips.
webcam.lead: Make sure your camera works and looks good. See the live picture, the real resolution and FPS, and take a snapshot in one click.

article.h: How to test your webcam
ol: Click "Start webcam test" and allow camera access.
Choose your camera and the resolution you want to check.
Look at the badges in the corner for the live resolution and FPS.
Take a snapshot or record a short clip to review sharpness and color.

article.h: Understanding resolution and FPS
p: Resolution is the number of pixels in each frame: 640 × 480 (480p), 1280 × 720 (720p HD), 1920 × 1080 (1080p Full HD) or 3840 × 2160 (4K). The test asks for the resolution you pick and shows what the camera actually delivers. Many webcams advertise 1080p but fall back to 720p in some browsers or under USB bandwidth limits.

FPS (frames per second) measures smoothness. 30 FPS is the standard for video calls and 60 FPS looks extra fluid. The FPS shown here is measured from real frames, not just reported by the driver, so it's a true picture of what others will see.

article.h: Camera not working or black screen?
ul: Close Zoom, Teams, Skype, OBS and any other tab using the camera. Most cameras can only be used by one app at a time.
Open the physical privacy shutter, or press the camera key (often F8, F10 or Fn+F-key) on laptops.
Windows 10/11: Settings → Privacy & security → Camera → turn on "Camera access" and "Let apps access your camera".
macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Camera → enable your browser.
iPhone / iPad: Settings → Safari → Camera → Allow. Android: App info → Permissions → Camera.
Pick a lower resolution if the picture freezes, and plug USB cameras straight into the computer rather than a hub.

article.h: Look better on video calls
ul: Face a window or a soft lamp. Light from behind turns you into a silhouette.
Raise the camera to eye level and use the grid to frame your eyes on the top third line.
Low FPS in the evening? Add light. Webcams lengthen their exposure in the dark, which lowers the frame rate.
Clean the lens: a fingerprint is the most common cause of a "soft" or hazy picture.

faq.q: How do I check if my webcam works?
faq.a: Click "Start webcam test" and allow access. If you see yourself and the status turns green, the camera works. The badges show the real resolution and FPS.

faq.q: Is a webcam test the same as a camera test or cam test?
faq.a: Yes. Webcam test, camera test and cam test all mean the same thing here: checking that your camera turns on, how sharp the picture is and how smooth the video runs.

faq.q: Why is the picture mirrored?
faq.a: Front cameras are mirrored by default because that feels natural, like a mirror. Others on a call see you unmirrored. Use the Mirror button to switch.

faq.q: Why is my webcam FPS low?
faq.a: Usually low light, a busy USB port or a high resolution. Add light, choose 720p, or connect the camera directly to the computer.

faq.q: Can I test my phone's front and back cameras?
faq.a: Yes. Open this page on your phone and tap "Switch camera" to toggle between the front and rear cameras.

faq.q: Are my snapshots uploaded?
faq.a: No. Snapshots and clips are created in your browser and only saved if you download them.

speaker.title: Speaker Test: Left/Right Audio & Headphone Test Online
speaker.description: Speaker test and headphone test online. Play left, right and center tones, adjust the frequency and run a 40 Hz to 16 kHz sweep for bass and treble.
speaker.lead: Check that your speakers and headphones work, that left and right aren't swapped, and how far your hearing and gear reach.

article.h: How to test your speakers or headphones
ol: Set your system volume to a comfortable, low level.
Press Left, then Right. Each sound should come only from that side.
Press Both to check the center image.
Run the frequency sweep to hear the range from deep bass to high treble.

article.h: Left and right swapped or missing?
p: If the left tone plays on the right, your headphones are on backwards or a cable or adapter is wired in reverse. If one side is silent, check the balance slider in your sound settings (Windows: Settings → System → Sound → your device → Left/Right; macOS: System Settings → Sound → Output → Balance), then try another cable or port.
Some phones and laptops use a single mono speaker. In that case Left and Right both come out of the same place, and that is expected.

article.h: The frequency sweep and your hearing
p: Young people can typically hear from about 20 Hz to 20 kHz. The upper limit falls with age, and many adults stop hearing tones above 14–16 kHz. Small laptop and phone speakers often can't reproduce much below 100–150 Hz, so the start of the sweep may be silent on them even though your hearing is fine. Keep the volume low: high-frequency tones can be uncomfortable.

article.h: No sound at all?
ul: Check that the system and browser tab aren't muted. Look for a crossed-out speaker icon on the tab.
Make sure the right output device is selected (Bluetooth headphones often take over automatically).
Unplug and reconnect wired headphones, or re-pair Bluetooth ones.
On iPhone, turn off Silent mode. On Android, raise the media volume rather than the ringer.

faq.q: How do I test left and right speakers?
faq.a: Press the Left button. The tone should play only from the left side. Then press Right. If they're reversed, swap your headphones or check the cable and balance settings.

faq.q: Why can't I hear the high frequencies?
faq.a: Hearing above 15 kHz naturally decreases with age, and many small speakers can't play very high or very low frequencies. Both are normal.

faq.q: Is the test tone safe for my ears?
faq.a: Yes at normal volume. Start with low system volume and turn it up gradually, especially with headphones.

faq.q: Does it work with Bluetooth headphones?
faq.a: Yes. Connect them first so they become the active output, then play the tones.

card.name: Discord mic test
card.desc: Check your mic before you join voice.

discord.title: Discord Mic Test: Check Your Microphone Before Voice Chat
discord.description: Free Discord mic test. Check your mic level, hear yourself back and fix the Discord settings that stop friends from hearing you. Runs in your browser.
discord.lead: Make sure your mic works before you hop into a voice channel. Test it here, then match the same settings in Discord.

article.h: How to test your mic for Discord
ol: Press "Start mic test" and allow microphone access.
Pick the same microphone you use in Discord from the drop-down.
Talk at your normal volume and watch the level meter.
Record 5 seconds and play it back to hear what your friends hear.

article.h: Mic works here but not in Discord?
p: If the meter moves on this page, your microphone and your system are fine. The problem is a Discord setting. Open User Settings (the gear next to your name) → Voice & Video and check these, in order:
ul: Input Device: choose your microphone by name instead of "Default". Discord often stays on an old default after you plug in a headset.
Input Sensitivity: turn off "Automatically determine input sensitivity" and drag the slider left until your voice lights up the bar.
Input Mode: if you use Push to Talk, check the keybind. Holding the wrong key looks exactly like a dead mic.
A red mic icon with a slash next to your name means you are server muted. Only a moderator can undo that.
If your voice cuts in and out, set Noise Suppression to None for a moment and test again.
Still nothing? Scroll down and press "Reset Voice Settings", then pick your mic again.

article.h: Getting a clean sound on Discord
p: Aim for speech that peaks between −20 dB and −10 dB on the meter here. Lower than that and friends will turn you up and hear your fan. Higher than that and you will clip when you laugh or shout. If you play without headphones, keep Echo Cancellation on in Discord so your speakers don't feed back into the mic.

faq.q: Why can't my friends hear me on Discord?
faq.a: Usually Discord is listening to a different device, the input sensitivity is set too high, or you are muted. Pick your mic by name in Voice & Video, lower the sensitivity and check the mic icon next to your name.

faq.q: How do I test my mic inside Discord?
faq.a: Go to User Settings → Voice & Video and press "Let's Check" under Mic Test. The bar should move while you talk.

faq.q: Does Discord work with USB and Bluetooth mics?
faq.a: Yes. Connect the mic, then select it by name in Discord's Input Device list. Bluetooth headsets may switch to a lower quality mode while the mic is in use, which is normal.

faq.q: Is this test connected to my Discord account?
faq.a: No. This page runs in your browser and never talks to Discord. Nothing is uploaded.

card.name: Zoom mic test
card.desc: Be ready before your next meeting.

zoom.title: Zoom Mic Test: Check Your Microphone Before a Meeting
zoom.description: Test your microphone before a Zoom call. Check the level, record and listen back, then fix the Zoom audio settings that make you sound quiet or silent.
zoom.lead: Thirty seconds here saves the "can you hear me?" at the start of every meeting. Test your mic, then check the same settings in Zoom.

article.h: How to test your mic before a Zoom call
ol: Press "Start mic test" and allow microphone access.
Choose the microphone you will use in the meeting.
Speak normally. The meter should reach the green zone.
Record a short clip and listen to it with headphones.

article.h: Zoom audio settings that matter
ul: Settings → Audio → Microphone: pick your mic by name and press "Test Mic".
If your volume keeps drifting, untick "Automatically adjust microphone volume" and set the slider yourself.
"Suppress background noise" on Auto works for most rooms. Set it to Low if your voice sounds choppy.
Playing music or teaching an instrument? Turn on "Original sound for musicians" so Zoom stops filtering your audio.

article.h: Nobody can hear you in the meeting?
ul: Check the microphone icon at the bottom left. A red line means you are muted.
If you see "Join Audio" instead of a mic icon, click it and choose "Join with Computer Audio".
The host may have muted everyone. Ask in the chat or press "Raise Hand".
Close other apps that use the mic, such as Teams, Discord or another browser tab, then rejoin.

faq.q: How do I test my mic before a Zoom meeting?
faq.a: Use the mic test on this page, or open Zoom's Settings → Audio → Test Mic. Zoom also offers a test meeting at zoom.us/test.

faq.q: Why does Zoom say my microphone is not available?
faq.a: Another app is probably using it, or Zoom has no permission. Close other call apps and allow Zoom in your system's microphone privacy settings.

faq.q: Why do I sound quiet on Zoom?
faq.a: The system input volume is low or Zoom's automatic volume pulled it down. Raise the input volume and untick automatic adjustment in Zoom.

faq.q: Does this page record or send my audio?
faq.a: No. Everything runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.

card.name: iPhone mic test
card.desc: Check your iPhone microphones in Safari.

iphone.title: iPhone Mic Test: Check Your iPhone Microphone Online
iphone.description: Test your iPhone microphone in Safari, no app needed. See the live level, record and play back, and fix the iOS settings that block the mic.
iphone.lead: Open this page in Safari or Chrome on your iPhone, allow the microphone and speak. You'll know in seconds whether the mic works.

article.h: How to test your iPhone microphone
ol: Open this page in Safari (or Chrome) on your iPhone.
Tap "Start mic test" and choose Allow when iOS asks.
Speak normally and watch the level meter.
Tap "Record 5s", then play it back to hear the quality.

article.h: Your iPhone has more than one microphone
p: Most iPhones have a microphone at the bottom next to the charging port, one in the earpiece at the top and one near the rear camera. Calls and voice memos mostly use the bottom mic, while video recording uses the others. If the meter barely moves, try speaking toward the bottom edge of the phone, and check that your case doesn't cover the small mic holes.

article.h: iPhone microphone not working?
ul: Website permission: in Safari, tap the "aA" button in the address bar → Website Settings → Microphone → Allow.
App permission: Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, and make sure your browser or app is switched on.
Bluetooth: AirPods or a car system can take over the mic. Turn Bluetooth off and test again.
Clean the mic holes gently with a soft dry brush. Never push anything sharp into them.
Restart the iPhone. If the Voice Memos app also records silence, contact Apple Support.

faq.q: Can I test my iPhone mic without an app?
faq.a: Yes. This page works in Safari and Chrome on iOS. Allow microphone access when asked and start the test.

faq.q: Why does my iPhone mic sound muffled?
faq.a: A case, screen protector edge or lint often covers the mic holes. Remove the case and gently clean the holes, then test again.

faq.q: Why can't people hear me on calls but the test works?
faq.a: Calls may route through a connected Bluetooth device or the earpiece mic. Disconnect Bluetooth and try speakerphone to compare.

faq.q: Is my recording uploaded?
faq.a: No. Recordings stay in Safari's memory until you close the page, unless you download them.

card.name: Android mic test
card.desc: Check your phone's mic in Chrome.

android.title: Android Mic Test: Check Your Phone Microphone Online
android.description: Test your Android microphone in Chrome, no app needed. See the live level, record and play back, and fix the Android settings that block the mic.
android.lead: Open this page in Chrome or Samsung Internet on your phone, allow the microphone and speak. The meter shows right away whether the mic picks you up.

article.h: How to test your Android microphone
ol: Open this page in Chrome, Samsung Internet or Firefox.
Tap "Start mic test" and allow microphone access.
Speak normally and watch the level meter.
Record 5 seconds and play it back to judge the quality.

article.h: Android microphone not working?
ul: Quick Settings: swipe down and make sure the "Microphone access" tile is on (Android 12 and later).
Browser permission: tap the icon left of the address → Permissions → Microphone → Allow.
App permission: Settings → Apps → Chrome → Permissions → Microphone → Allow only while using the app.
Bluetooth earbuds or a smartwatch can take over the mic. Turn Bluetooth off and test again.
Remove the case and clean the small mic hole at the bottom gently with a soft dry brush.
Restart the phone. If the built-in recorder app also records silence, the mic hardware may need repair.

article.h: Why calls sound different from this test
p: During calls, Android uses noise cancellation and often a second mic at the top of the phone to remove background sound. Browser recordings use a lighter version of the same processing. If the test sounds clear but calls don't, check your carrier's Wi-Fi Calling or VoLTE settings, or try a call with speakerphone on.

faq.q: Can I test my phone mic without installing an app?
faq.a: Yes. This page works in Chrome, Samsung Internet and Firefox on Android. Allow microphone access and start the test.

faq.q: Why is my Android mic blocked in the browser?
faq.a: Either the browser has no microphone permission or the Microphone access toggle in Quick Settings is off. Turn both on and reload the page.

faq.q: Does it work on Samsung phones?
faq.a: Yes. Use Samsung Internet or Chrome. On Samsung phones you'll find app permissions under Settings → Apps → Permissions.

faq.q: Is my audio uploaded?
faq.a: No. Everything happens on your phone and nothing is sent to a server.

card.name: AirPods mic test
card.desc: Check the mic in your AirPods.

airpods.title: AirPods Mic Test: Check Your AirPods Microphone Online
airpods.description: Test the microphone in your AirPods on iPhone, Mac or Windows. Pick AirPods as input, check the level and fix the settings that make them sound bad.
airpods.lead: Connect your AirPods, select them in the microphone list and speak. The meter and a quick recording tell you if the AirPods mic works and how it sounds.

article.h: How to test your AirPods microphone
ol: Put your AirPods in and connect them to your device.
Press "Start mic test" and allow microphone access.
Choose your AirPods in the microphone drop-down.
Talk normally, then record 5 seconds and play it back.

article.h: Choosing AirPods as the microphone
ul: iPhone: AirPods are used automatically once connected. Open this page in Safari and allow the microphone.
Mac: open System Settings → Sound → Input and select your AirPods.
Windows: AirPods appear twice, as "Headphones" and "Headset". Pick the "Headset" entry as your input, or the mic won't work.
Only one ear? On iPhone go to Settings → Bluetooth → the ⓘ next to your AirPods → Microphone, and choose Automatic, Always Left or Always Right.

article.h: Why AirPods sound worse on calls
p: When the microphone is active, Bluetooth switches to a hands-free mode that carries audio in both directions at a lower quality. That's why music sounds great but calls sound thin, especially on Windows and Android. It's normal behavior, not a fault. For the best voice quality in long calls on a computer, a wired or USB microphone still beats any Bluetooth earbuds.

faq.q: Why doesn't my AirPods mic work on Windows?
faq.a: Windows lists AirPods twice. Select the "Headset" device as your input in Settings → System → Sound, and in your call app.

faq.q: Why does the AirPods mic sound muffled?
faq.a: Dirt in the mic grille at the bottom of the stem is the most common cause. Clean it gently with a dry cotton swab.

faq.q: Can I use only one AirPod as a mic?
faq.a: Yes. On iPhone, set Microphone to Always Left or Always Right in the AirPods Bluetooth settings.

faq.q: Is my audio uploaded?
faq.a: No. The test runs in your browser and nothing leaves your device.

headphone.title: Headphone Test: Left/Right, Stereo and Bass Check Online
headphone.description: Free online headphone test. Check left and right channels, stereo balance and bass with test tones and a frequency sweep. Works with wired and Bluetooth.
headphone.lead: Find out in seconds if both sides of your headphones work, if left and right are the right way round, and how deep the bass goes.

article.h: How to test your headphones
ol: Put your headphones on and turn the volume down to a comfortable level.
Press Left: the tone should come only from your left ear. Then press Right.
Press Both: the tone should sound centered, in the middle of your head.
Run the frequency sweep to hear the range from deep bass to high treble.

article.h: One side quieter or silent?
ul: Check the balance slider: Windows Settings → System → Sound → your device → Left/Right, or on a Mac System Settings → Sound → Output → Balance.
On iPhone, make sure Mono Audio is off: Settings → Accessibility → Audio & Visual.
Wired headphones: unplug, clean the plug and push it in fully. A half-inserted plug often kills one side.
Earwax on the mesh is a common cause of one quiet earbud. Clean it gently with a dry brush.

article.h: Bass, treble and Bluetooth
p: Good over-ear headphones play clearly down to 30 or 40 Hz at the start of the sweep. Small earbuds need a tight seal to produce bass, so try a larger ear tip if the low end sounds thin. Bluetooth adds a short delay, usually 100 to 250 milliseconds, which doesn't matter for music but is noticeable in games.

faq.q: How do I know if my headphones are left/right reversed?
faq.a: Press Left. If the sound comes from your right ear, the headphones are on backwards or the cable or adapter is wired in reverse.

faq.q: Why can't I hear the start of the sweep?
faq.a: Very low notes need a good seal and bigger drivers. Many earbuds and laptop speakers can't play much below 100 Hz.

faq.q: Is the test safe for my ears?
faq.a: Yes at a normal volume. Start low and turn it up slowly, especially with in-ear headphones.

faq.q: Does it work with Bluetooth headphones?
faq.a: Yes. Connect them first so they become the active output, then play the tones.

recorder.title: Online Voice Recorder: Record Audio Free, No Sign-up
recorder.description: Free online voice recorder. Record your voice in the browser, play it back and download the file. No time limit, no sign-up, nothing is uploaded.
recorder.lead: Record your voice right in the browser and download the file. No sign-up, no time limit, and the audio never leaves your device.

article.h: How to record your voice online
ol: Press "Start recording" and allow microphone access.
Choose your microphone if you have more than one.
Speak, sing or play. The timer and level meter show that it's working.
Press Stop. Your recording appears below, ready to play or download.

article.h: What file do I get?
p: Chrome, Edge and Firefox save WebM audio with the Opus codec. Safari saves an M4A (AAC) file. Both play in VLC, most media players and editors like Audacity. If you need an MP3, any audio converter can change the format in a few seconds.

article.h: Tips for a better recording
ul: Run the mic test first and aim for peaks between −20 dB and −10 dB.
Record in a small room with soft furniture. Curtains and a sofa cut echo more than any filter.
Keep the microphone about a hand's width from your mouth and slightly to the side.
Turn off fans and notifications, and use headphones if you play a backing track.

faq.q: Is there a time limit?
faq.a: No fixed limit. Recordings are kept in your browser's memory, so very long sessions depend on your device. For recordings over an hour, download in parts.

faq.q: Where are my recordings saved?
faq.a: Only in this browser tab until you download them. Closing or reloading the page deletes them.

faq.q: Does it work on iPhone and Android?
faq.a: Yes. It works in Safari on iPhone and in Chrome or Samsung Internet on Android.

faq.q: Is the voice recorder really free?
faq.a: Yes. No sign-up, no watermark and no upload.
